prompt:
You are a careful equity research analyst. Assess the competitive advantages (economic moat) and pricing power of the publicly listed company "Eaton Corp plc" (ticker ETN), and list its competitors. Use the most recent information you know. Never invent figures: use null when unsure. Be specific (products, numbers, years).

Reply with ONLY one JSON object, no other text, in exactly this shape:
{
 "name": "official company name", "ticker": "ETN", "industry": "industry in a few words",
 "markets": ["the main product markets it competes in"],
 "mission": {"statement": "the company's own official mission statement, word for word as it publishes it; null if you are not sure of the exact wording (never paraphrase here)",
             "source": "where it is published, e.g. company website or 2025 annual report, or null",
             "plain": "what the mission means, in one short simple sentence"},
 "about": {"plain": "3-4 short sentences explaining what the company does, in simple everyday words a 12-year-old would understand; no jargon",
           "customers": "who buys from it, in one simple sentence",
           "everyday": "one sentence linking it to something ordinary people know or use, or null",
           "money": [ {"part": "business line in simple words", "share": decimal share of sales or null, "plain": "what it sells there, in a few simple words", "tag": "main|new|moonshot"} ]  (its main ways of making money, largest first, up to 6; also include any new business line or one with explosive, moonshot potential even if its sales are still small. tag: "main" = an established line that brings in a large part of sales; "new" = launched or entered in roughly the last 3 years; "moonshot" = could grow many times over or reshape the company, e.g. a new technology or market, even if unproven. Give each line one tag, the one that fits best)},
 "summary": "2-3 plain-English sentences on whether and why it has a competitive advantage",
 "pricingPower": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "specific evidence, e.g. price rises and what happened to volumes"},
 "moats": [ {"source": one of ["Brand and intangible assets","Switching costs","Network effects","Cost advantage and scale","Efficient scale","Counter-positioning","Process power (hard-to-copy know-how)","Cornered resource (exclusive asset or talent)"], "strength": "strong|moderate|weak|none", "evidence": "one or two specific sentences"} ]  (all 8 sources, in that order),
 "customers": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "customer satisfaction and loyalty: retention, NPS, reviews, repeat purchase"},
 "talent": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "ability to attract and keep top talent: employer rankings, reputation, pay"},
 "product": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "is the product best in class? independent benchmarks, awards, ecosystem"},
 "competitors": [ {"name": "company name", "ticker": "main listing ticker (exchange suffix if not US, e.g. 005930.KS) or null if private",
                   "usTicker": "ticker of its US listing or ADR that files reports with the SEC, or null", "overlap": "high|medium|low",
                   "note": "where they compete"} ]  (every significant competitor, most direct first, up to 15; include major private ones with ticker null),
 "estimates": [ {"name": "company name", "fy": "FY2025", "currency": "USD", "revenueUSDm": number, "revenueGrowth3y": decimal, "grossMargin": decimal, "operatingMargin": decimal, "netMargin": decimal} ]
   (approximate latest fiscal-year figures for the company itself and for every listed competitor; decimals, e.g. 0.42; null if unknown),
 "marketShare": [ {"market": "market name", "measure": "revenue|units|shipments|...", "latestYear": "2025", "earlierYear": "2020",
                   "rows": [ {"name": "company name", "latest": decimal or null, "earlier": decimal or null} ] } ]  (up to 3 of its main markets, the company and its main rivals),
 "threats": ["specific things that could weaken its advantage"],
 "ceo": {"name": "current CEO", "founder": true or false, "since": "YYYY", "background": "e.g. electrical engineer, Stanford MBA"},
 "checklist": { "<id>": {"verdict": "yes|partly|no|unknown", "evidence": "one specific sentence with names, numbers or examples"} }  for EVERY id below:
   "c1": Rule Breaker #1: is it the leader of an important industry that is still emerging and growing fast?
   "c2": Rule Breaker #2: why do customers choose it over rivals (brand, better value, innovation, culture, leadership), and is that advantage hard to copy and likely to last many years?
   "c3": Rule Breaker #5: do ordinary people recognise the name, is it the default leader in its field (like Google, Amazon, NVIDIA, Tesla, Intuitive Surgical, Netflix), and would customers recommend its product?
   "c4": Does it have an inspiring mission it keeps emphasising, with management driven by purpose rather than money? If it spends 10 years doing this, would it matter?
   "c6": What is the general public consensus about the company and its products or services? When people hear the name, what are the first few descriptive words that come to mind? Start the evidence with those words in quotes (e.g. “innovative, premium, reliable”), then say whether that impression is mostly positive.
   "c7": Is its total addressable market large and growing, riding a secular trend (like CRWD, NVDA, TSLA, AMZN)?
   "c8": Does it have room to expand into big new markets: in its name, its technology or its vision?
   "m1": Is the CEO a visionary with a clear picture of the future?
   "m2": Is the CEO a founder (or acting like one): long-term thinking, working extraordinarily hard, pouring heart and soul into building something that outlives them?
   "m4": Does the CEO lead by serving employees and customers?
   "m5": Has the CEO deliberately built a strong, distinctive culture that keeps inventing new products and technologies?
   "m6": Is the CEO deeply hands-on with the product and technology, ideally with an engineering background?
   "m7": Is the CEO a person of great character who cares about something bigger than profit? For successor CEOs: is stewardship aimed at the benefit of humanity?
   "m7b": Has the CEO been invited to give a commencement speech at a top university (Stanford, Harvard, MIT, etc.)? Name it.
   "m8b": Does the CEO have a distinctive, memorable personality (like Elon Musk, Alex Karp, Larry Page)?
   "m9": Has the CEO a strong record of execution and results?
   "m10": Is the CEO and company known for frugality (like Bezos's door desk)?
   "c10": Do its products solve problems for people all over the world, greatly improving the lives of a very large number of people (like NFLX, GOOG, ISRG)?
   "p2": Is what it builds extremely hard to do, and important to the world?
   "f1": Has revenue grown in almost every one of the last five years?
   "f2": Have gross and operating margins risen over the last five years?
   "f3": Is debt low compared with cash and cash flow, with positive shareholders' equity?
   "f4": Have operating income and operating cash flow risen over the last five years?
   "v1": Is its main product clearly the best in its field, with a practical reason an ordinary person can understand for choosing it over every alternative (like NVIDIA over AMD)?
   "v2": Is it widely seen as one of the best companies to work for (culture, mission, reputation, employer rankings)? Cite rankings.
   "c5": Do its products make the world better? If it disappeared overnight, who would notice and miss it, and why?
 "asOf": "YYYY-MM of the newest information you used"
}

result.name: Eaton Corporation plc
result.industry: Electrical power management equipment and aerospace systems
markets: Electrical distribution and power quality equipment (switchgear, breakers, UPS, power distribution) for data centers, utilities, commercial and industrial buildings
Data center power and liquid cooling (grid-to-chip)
Utility and grid equipment (transformers, prefabricated power modules)
Aerospace fuel, hydraulic, power and thermal systems
Commercial vehicle and light vehicle drivetrain components (Mobility, being spun off)
eMobility power electronics and EV components

mission.statement: To improve the quality of life and the environment through the use of power management technologies and services.
mission.source: Eaton company materials (mission statement as published on its company profiles and sustainability materials)
mission.plain: Eaton wants to make life better and cleaner by helping the world use electric power more safely and efficiently.

about.plain: Eaton makes the equipment that moves electricity safely from the power grid into buildings, factories and huge computer centers. Think of big switch boxes, circuit breakers, backup batteries and now liquid cooling for computer chips. It also makes parts for airplanes, like fuel and hydraulic systems, and parts for trucks and cars. Its biggest growth today comes from the giant data centers being built for artificial intelligence.
about.customers: Data center builders and cloud companies, electric utilities, building contractors and electrical distributors, factories, aircraft makers and airlines, and truck and car makers.
about.everyday: The breaker panel and surge protector in many homes and offices, and the backup power that keeps websites and apps running, are often Eaton products.

money.plain: switchgear, breakers, UPS and power systems for data centers, utilities and buildings in North and South America
the same kinds of electrical gear sold in Europe, Asia and elsewhere, now including Boyd Thermal liquid cooling
fuel, hydraulic, power and thermal systems for planes and defense
transmissions, clutches and valvetrain parts for trucks and cars (part of the Mobility spin-off)

money.part: Data center liquid cooling (Boyd Thermal, acquired March 2026)
money.plain: coolant distribution units and cold plates that cool AI chips; about $1.5B of expected 2026 sales
power electronics and electrical parts for electric vehicles (part of the Mobility spin-off)

result.summary: Eaton has a solid, durable advantage built on a trusted brand with electrical contractors and distributors, a huge installed base of switchgear and power equipment that creates replacement and service demand, deep engineering know-how in safety-certified products, and the scale to add factory capacity fast for data centers and utilities. Its edge is real but not unique: Schneider Electric, ABB, Siemens and Vertiv offer similar products, so the moat is moderate-to-strong rather than monopoly-like. Gross margin rising from 30.5% (2020) to 37.6% (2025) suggests its position has strengthened.

pricingPower.evidence: Eaton raised prices through the 2021-2023 inflation while sales kept growing every year; gross margin rose from 30.5% in 2020 to 38.2% in 2024 and 37.6% in 2025, segment margin reached a record 24.5% in 2025, and Electrical Americas backlog was up 33% year on year in June 2026 with rolling orders up 41% organically, so demand outstrips supply.

moats.evidence: Eaton, Cutler-Hammer, Bussmann and Power Xpert are long-trusted names among electricians, engineers and specifiers, and UL-certified, code-compliant product lines take years to qualify; the brand is strong in the trade but not with consumers.

Once an engineer specifies Eaton switchgear and power distribution in a building or data center design, replacement parts, service and expansions tend to stay with the same vendor, and aerospace parts are certified on platforms for decades; new projects can still be re-bid against Schneider, ABB or Siemens.
Buying Eaton equipment does not make it more valuable for other customers; there is no meaningful network effect.

With $27.4B of 2025 sales and a global factory and distributor network, Eaton can fund capacity expansions and acquisitions such as Boyd Thermal ($9.5B) and Fibrebond ($1.4B) that smaller rivals cannot, but its three large European peers have similar scale.

North American electrical distribution equipment is concentrated among a few certified suppliers (Eaton, Schneider/Square D, Siemens, ABB/GE Industrial), and long lead times for switchgear and transformers make new entry hard.
Its grid-to-chip strategy (power plus liquid cooling) is similar to what Schneider (with Motivair) and Vertiv already do, so incumbents are not structurally prevented from copying it.

Decades of experience designing safety-critical arc-flash-resistant switchgear, UPS systems and aerospace fuel systems, plus its Eaton Business System operating model, lifted segment margins from about 22% in 2023 to 24.5% in 2025.
Eaton has no exclusive asset; it does hold long-term aerospace platform positions and data center capacity agreements, but competitors can obtain similar ones.

customers.evidence: Customers are committing years ahead: Electrical Americas backlog rose 31% in 2025 and 33% year on year by June 2026, Electrical Global backlog rose 103% (helped by Boyd), and Aerospace backlog rose 28%; no public NPS or retention figures are disclosed.

talent.evidence: Eaton was named one of Ethisphere's World's Most Ethical Companies for the 15th time in March 2026 and is a well-regarded engineering employer, but it is not a fixture of top best-places-to-work lists and pay is typical for industrials.

product.evidence: Eaton is one of the few full-line suppliers of low- and medium-voltage power distribution, UPS and power quality equipment, and with Boyd Thermal it now offers liquid cooling for AI chips; independent benchmarks are scarce, but its products are a default choice alongside Schneider, Siemens and ABB in North America.

threats: A slowdown or pause in AI data center construction, which drives much of Electrical Americas' order growth and backlog
Hyperscalers moving to new power architectures (such as 800V DC and solid-state transformers) where newer specialists or Asian suppliers (Delta, Huawei, LS Electric) could gain share
Integration risk and high price of the $9.5B Boyd Thermal deal (22.5x estimated 2026 adjusted EBITDA), which pushed total debt to about $20.6B by June 2026 and lowered Q2 2026 segment margin by 80 bp
Capacity additions across Schneider, Siemens, ABB, Vertiv and others could end today's equipment shortage and pressure pricing
Tariffs and copper and steel cost inflation
Execution risk in the planned spin-off of the Mobility (Vehicle and eMobility) business by the end of Q1 2027

ceo.name: Paulo Ruiz
ceo.background: Electrical engineer (FEI, Sao Paulo), master's in business management from Fundacao Dom Cabral; former CEO of Siemens' Dresser-Rand business, joined Eaton in 2019 and ran its Industrial Sector before becoming CEO on June 1, 2025

c1.evidence: Eaton is one of the top four suppliers of electrical power equipment for fast-growing AI data centers (Electrical Americas rolling orders up 41% organically in Q2 2026), but the wider electrical equipment industry is over a century old rather than emerging.

c2.evidence: Customers pick Eaton for a full line of certified power gear, delivery capacity and service on a large installed base, and now grid-to-chip packages with Boyd liquid cooling; these advantages last but Schneider, Siemens, ABB and Vertiv offer similar ones.

c3.evidence: Eaton is well known to electricians and engineers but few ordinary consumers recognize it, and it shares leadership with Schneider Electric rather than being the single default name.

c4.evidence: Its mission 'to improve the quality of life and the environment through the use of power management technologies and services' is sensible and repeated in its sustainability reporting, but management messaging centers on margins, orders and EPS rather than a purpose-driven crusade.

c6.evidence: “industrial, reliable, electrical, data-center play”: those who know the name see a dependable, well-run power-equipment maker, and the impression is mostly positive.

c7.evidence: Electrification, AI data centers, grid upgrades and reshoring are secular trends lifting Eaton's backlog (Electrical Americas up 33% and Electrical Global up 103% year on year at June 2026).

c8.evidence: The Boyd Thermal deal ($1.7B of expected 2026 sales, $1.5B in liquid cooling) moved Eaton into data center cooling, and it is extending into prefabricated power modules (Fibrebond) and DC power (Resilient Power Systems).

m1.evidence: Paulo Ruiz has set out a clear 'grid to chip' data center vision and reshaped the portfolio with Boyd, Ultra PCS and the Mobility spin-off, but he is an operator-strategist rather than a celebrated visionary.

m2.evidence: Ruiz is a professional manager who became CEO in June 2025 after a planned succession; Eaton has a mandatory officer retirement age of 65, typical of a long-established company.

m4.evidence: There is no clear public evidence either way about Ruiz's servant-leadership style beyond Eaton's stated values of developing employees and delighting customers.

m5.evidence: Eaton has a long-standing ethics-focused culture (15 Ethisphere recognitions) and the Eaton Business System, but its growth relies heavily on acquisitions rather than a culture known for breakthrough invention.

m6.evidence: Ruiz holds an electrical engineering degree and began in engineering and operations at Fiat, though his recent career has been general management.

m7.evidence: There are no controversies, but there is too little public record of Ruiz's personal causes to judge his character beyond Eaton's ethics reputation.

m7b.evidence: No record found of Paulo Ruiz giving a commencement speech at a top university.

m8b.evidence: Ruiz keeps a low public profile typical of industrial CEOs.

m9.evidence: Before becoming CEO he led the Industrial Sector's portfolio and margin improvements, and in his first full year Eaton posted record 2025 sales of $27.4B and adjusted EPS of $12.07 (up 12%), then raised 2026 organic growth guidance to 11-13%.

m10.evidence: Eaton is known for operational discipline but has no notable public reputation for frugality.

c10.evidence: Its equipment quietly keeps power flowing to hospitals, data centers, factories and aircraft worldwide, which benefits huge numbers of people indirectly rather than as a life-changing consumer product.

p2.evidence: Safety-certified switchgear, UPS and aerospace fuel systems are important and require deep know-how, but several large competitors can build comparable products.

f2.evidence: Gross margin rose from 30.5% (2020) to 37.6% (2025) and pre-tax income plus interest rose from 10.6% to 18.8% of sales, though gross margin dipped slightly from 38.2% in 2024.

f3.evidence: Equity is positive at $20.3B, but after the Boyd and Ultra PCS deals total debt reached $20.6B against $695M of cash and short-term investments at June 30, 2026, about 5.8 times 2025 free cash flow of $3,553M.

f4.evidence: Pre-tax income plus interest rose every year from $1,895M (2020) to $5,173M (2025), and operating cash flow rose from $2,944M (2020) to $4,472M (2025) but dipped to $2,163M in 2021.

v1.evidence: Eaton is a top choice in electrical gear but there is no simple reason to pick it over Schneider, Siemens or ABB in every case; customers often choose on delivery time, price and existing relationships.

v2.evidence: Eaton was named one of Ethisphere's World's Most Ethical Companies for the 15th time in 2026, but it does not rank near the top of best-places-to-work lists like Glassdoor's or Fortune's 100 Best.

c5.evidence: If Eaton vanished, data center operators, utilities, contractors and aircraft makers would face equipment shortages and delays, but rivals could eventually replace most of its products.
